messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhang <claire@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cruise Control: ops snapshot, QBR asks & open decisions

Team —

Quick weekly snapshot ahead of Friday's QBR prep call. I kept this short; pulling the key wins, risks, and concrete asks so leadership can triage. If you want deeper slides ping me and I’ll attach the longer deck.

Wins
- Hosted API latency SLOs: 95th p99 improved to 180ms for the primary gen route after kernel update (seen in CI and staging).
- Dedicated pilot: Acme POC completed inference load test at committed throughput (20k tokens/sec) with 98% success rate.
- Observability: Trace sampling rollout reached 100% for customer-critical routes; early traces caught a tokenization mismatch (fixed).

Risks / Open blockers
- SLA ask from Acme procurement: They want a 99.99% uptime SLA and data residency guarantee for EU. Legal + Infra need to align before we sign. (Request attached: SLA-request-10.24.docx)
- Backend capacity: Peak concurrency for embeddings batchers spiked 2.4x last night — autoscale config tolerated it but cost jumped. Need cost guardrails before wider rollout to mid-market.
- QBR metric gap: We still lack a stable baseline for per-route unit cost (tokens + infra) for Dedicated customers. Ops needs 1 week to finalize.

Asks (concrete, owners, and due dates)
- Laura: sign-off on the exception to the residency policy for Acme's EU pilot by EOD Thursday if legal review is green.
- Jonas: recommend a temporary guardrail (hard cap on autoscale increments) and a short doc on rollback criteria by Thursday COB.
- Marissa: coordinate a one-hour sync with Acme procurement + Legal next Tues; suggested attendees in the draft invite.
- All: review the attached short QBR slide (QBR_prep_slides_v2.pdf) and send edits by Thursday 3pm PT.

Next steps: I'll consolidate decisions and update the QBR one-pager before Friday's prep.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.com
[Attachment: QBR_prep_slides_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: SLA-request-10.24.docx]

Thanks, Ava — good concise breakdown. Two quick notes: 

1) On the Acme SLA/residency ask: Legal flagged that we can offer EU data residency for Dedicated but not for Hosted unless they sign a top-tier enterprise contract. I can draft the exception language.

2) Autoscale guardrail: I support a hard cap for the next 30 days; we should set the cap at +1.5x current baseline and add automated alerts at 1.2x. I'll put a tech note in Ops’ runbook and share by EOD Thursday.

Can you add a one-line impact statement to slide 3 (cost delta estimate) so leadership has a concrete number? I'll call out the proposed guardrail in the meeting.
